messages:
maria: Customer hit a CI break after we pushed a tagged release. Their app builds fine locally but CI fails with checksum/version mismatch. They use a local replace in go.mod to point at a fork. Repro steps attached.

maria: go.mod snippet:
```
module github.com/customer/app

require (
\tgithub.com/redwood/inference-sdk v1.2.0
)

replace github.com/redwood/inference-sdk => github.com/customer/inference-sdk v0.0.0-20250201010101-abcdef123456
```

maria: CI error (short):
```
verifying github.com/redwood/inference-sdk@v1.2.0: checksum mismatch
failed to download: v1.2.0: go: github.com/redwood/inference-sdk@v1.2.0: checksum mismatch
```

devon: hmm. So they have both require on v1.2.0 and replace to a pseudo-version — that should work locally if GOPRIVATE is set. Does CI set GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB?

maria: Their Dockerfile builds with `ENV GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer` but the repo path is github.com/redwood/inference-sdk replaced to github.com/customer/inference-sdk — might be a mismatch. CI uses `-mod=mod` (default).

chris: two hypotheses: (1) CI is still hitting proxy/sumdb for v1.2.0 before replace kicks in, causing checksum verification against upstream tag (which differs because upstream tag files changed), or (2) tagged release v1.2.0 was force-updated (rewritten) after publish, checksum mismatch results.

samir: Can we confirm whether upstream actually has v1.2.0 on tag vs pseudo? Run `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go list -m -json github.com/redwood/inference-sdk@v1.2.0` and also `go env -w GOSUMDB=off` (temporarily) to see if build proceeds.

maria: I ran two commands in a clean container:
```
# lists proxy info
GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go list -m -json github.com/redwood/inference-sdk@v1.2.0
# output shows Version: "v1.2.0" and Sum: "h1:xxxxxxxx"

# then with replace in go.mod, `go mod tidy` fetches the pseudo-version but verify still checks v1.2.0 sum and fails
```

devon: Ok reproduction looks consistent. Could be that replace directive using a pseudo-version with a different module path triggers sum mismatch because `go` checks the module version recorded for required module before it applies replace. Strange but plausible.

chris: Workaround for customer: pin the require to the pseudo-version instead of v1.2.0, e.g. `require github.com/redwood/inference-sdk v0.0.0-20250201010101-abcdef123456` and remove replace. Does that unblock CI?

maria: Customer tried pinning require -> it works locally but their CI enforces semver tags and will fail other workflows. They want to keep upstream semver in codebase.

samir: We should check our published v1.2.0 artifact on the proxy. Also confirm whether the upstream tag contains a go.mod with a `module` path identical to the replace target. If upstream v1.2.0's go.mod module path is different (e.g., module github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/v1) then go will canonicalize which can cause mismatch when replace points to unversioned path.

maria: I pulled the archive from the proxy and inspected go.mod in the v1.2.0 tag — it has `module github.com/redwood/inference-sdk` (no /v1). The forked replace package has same module path.

devon: Another angle: CI uses `GONOSUMDB` and `GOPROXY` envs? If CI sends modules through an internal proxy that cached a previous checksum, a later rewrite of upstream tag will cause a mismatch. Did the customer force-push the tag?

maria: Customer says they did not touch the upstream repo (redwood package) — they only maintain the fork. Our internal audit shows no force-push on redwood repo.

pkg-bot: :information_source: Detected that github.com/redwood/inference-sdk v1.2.0 was published 2025-11-03 14:22:10 UTC and checksum h1:xxxxxxxx recorded.

samir: Given the complexity, propose steps: (A) give customer a minimal reproducible Dockerfile & CI snippet to demonstrate behavior; (B) recommend setting GOPRIVATE to include both the fork and the original module path (GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer,github.com/redwood) so replace always resolves locally; (C) escalate to eng-runtime if we find any evidence our published artifact mismatched checksum.

maria: I'll send repro to customer and ask for CI logs for `go env` and `env | grep GOPRIVATE|GOPROXY|GOSUMDB`. Also I'll try pinning require in a temp branch to unblock them.

devon: If customer needs immediate unblock, suggest a temporary mirror: `replace github.com/redwood/inference-sdk => ../local/inference-sdk` (checkout the fork in workspace) and use a bind-mounted workspace in CI. Ugly but works.

chris: Filing a support bug for eng-runtime to verify published v1.2.0 artifact and check for any proxy cache anomalies. Bug refs: INF-SUP-4321.

maria: Thanks — I'll update thread when customer responds. :thumbsup:
